Brett Smith

Pacific Green candidate for Governor, Oregon · Challenger

Tradesman (former welder, mill worker and maintenance worker); inventor of a medical device

Brett Smith, 44, of Molalla, is the Pacific Green Party of Oregon's nominee for governor in the November 3, 2026 general election. He won the party's nomination over three other candidates. He has not held elected office and ran in 2024 as the Independent Party nominee for Oregon's 5th Congressional District.

Where Smith stands

Affordability and utility costs
Proposes a surcharge on large employers whose workers earn so little that they rely on public assistance. Says corporations should bear more of the cost of supporting their workforces.
Health care and food assistance
Proposes a surcharge on employers with 50 or more workers who pay below a living wage, with the money going to the Oregon Health Plan and food aid. His campaign models the revenue at $700 million to $3.4 billion a year.
Health care and food assistance
Supports universal health care.
Economy and jobs
Says taxes are the biggest burden on businesses. Calls for subsidizing small businesses instead of large ones.
Data centers
Says he would impose a permanent moratorium on data centers.
Federal administration
Proposes a state constitutional amendment protecting residents from drafts for wars that Congress has not authorized. Opposes Oregon ports handling weapons for such wars.
Immigration enforcement
Says he would expand the volunteer Oregon Civil Defense Force so the state can respond when federal agents act within Oregon. Pledges no unconstitutional surveillance.

Background

  • Pacific Green Party nominee for Oregon governor, 2026
  • Independent Party nominee for U.S. House, Oregon 5th District, 2024 (about 5% of the vote)
  • Has not held elected office
  • Former welder, mill worker and maintenance worker
  • Inventor of a medical device; holds multiple patents
  • Resident of Molalla, Oregon
